html:
SMTO-POL-0014 — This task has reached its limit on actions

GUID: 12265d2c-969a-4d32-bf8e-6787b7d98e04
Slug: tool-budget
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • Each task can take only a set number of actions, such as running commands. The next group of actions would have gone over that limit, so it didn't run. Earlier actions may already have made changes.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task in the conversation and look at its tool calls to see which actions finished. Actions completed before the limit already took effect and shouldn't be done twice.
  2. Check the actual files, computers or items the task was changing to confirm what is already done. The task's list shows what SMTO tried; the real files show what actually changed.
  3. Send a new message asking for only the work that is left, in smaller pieces, for example one folder at a time. A new task starts with a fresh action allowance, and smaller requests need fewer actions.

What success looks like

  • The new task finishes the remaining work without this message, and nothing was done twice.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If a small request also hits this limit, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to redo the whole task from the start; finished steps would run again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The pending tool batch or the unexecuted steps of a shell sequence need more concrete tool calls than remain in the run's tool allowance (tool_calls versus tool_limit), so they were rejected before execution.

What this means

  • The pending batch or unexecuted sequence suffix requires more concrete tool calls than the task has remaining. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The pending batch or unexecuted sequence suffix requires more concrete tool calls than the task has remaining.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the remaining concrete-call budget with unexecuted children and retained completed prefixes; model decision count is a different budget.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's tool_calls and tool_limit (native_max_tool_calls, default 10000) and its completed receipts (native/activities.py run_batch, native/shell_sequence.py). Continue only after confirming which effects already happened, with a smaller batch or a new request; model timeout or output-token changes don't add tool allowance.
  • Inspect completed receipts and report partial progress. Continue only through supported budget/task controls after checking outstanding effects; a model timeout change does not add tool allowance.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Any subsequently authorized continuation fits its concrete-call allowance while preserving completed child receipts.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
